findings.finding: the drill seed initially lacked agentId on sessions, which broke the turn path in PG form (MEMORY_AGENT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED). Real sessions carry agentId, and with it in the cochpia_state jsonb the turn commits (verified: 200, status=committed). Lesson recorded: seed/fixture data must mirror real shapes.

the PostgreSQL runtime read/write surface is a single cochpia_state jsonb row (store.js loadState/persist) — the normalized tables (cochpia_sessions/messages/...) are NOT in the runtime path; they are a reconciliation copy written by the migration script only. Rollback and accounting must be based on the jsonb, not the normalized tables.

normalized cochpia_sessions has no agent_id column and the migration script does not carry agentId into it — the reconciliation copy silently loses agent ownership (R-020 stage 2a concept never reached the legacy schema). Non-blocking because the runtime uses the jsonb, but nobody should trust the normalized copy for agent scoping.

the migration script hardcodes server/data/state.json and ignores COCHPIA_DATA_DIR — a real cutover must run from the deployment layout, and a COCHPIA_DATA_DIR-aware fix is advisable before any real run.

verdict: drill passed: migration, switch, window writes, export, rollback and read-back all verified on isolated copies
